teacher.subheadline: Strummy keeps every student's repertoire, lesson history, and progress in one place — so you walk into each lesson already knowing exactly where to pick up.
teacher.builtByPrefix: Built by a working guitar teacher —
teacher.builtBySuffix: used in his studio every day

student.subheadline: Strummy keeps your repertoire, practice history, and progress in one place — so you pick up the guitar already knowing exactly where to start, instead of guessing.
student.builtByPrefix: Built by a working guitar teacher —
student.builtBySuffix: also used by students who practice on their own

howItWorks.subheadline: Strummy fits the way a serious guitarist already thinks — whether you teach or practice on your own. You play — it keeps the record.
howItWorks.step1Body: Book lessons inside Strummy, or sync them straight from Google Calendar — both directions, automatically kept in step.
howItWorks.step2Body: Mark what each student played and how it's landing. Their repertoire and progress status advance forward on their own, never sliding back by accident.
howItWorks.step3Body: Before the lesson starts, last session's notes, their song list, and what to work on next are already on the screen.

dayInTheLife.headlinePrefix: You didn't get into teaching to manage
dayInTheLife.subheadline: Ask any working guitar teacher: hours every week disappear into admin nobody pays for. Here's what a normal day looks like.
dayInTheLife.before0: Dig through 6 WhatsApp threads to remember what Emma worked on last week.
dayInTheLife.before1: Email a parent a "progress update" you half-invent from memory.
dayInTheLife.before2: Can't find the tab for "Blackbird" you promised Carlos three weeks ago.
dayInTheLife.before3: Lesson starts. First ten minutes: catching up on your own notes.
dayInTheLife.before4: Tonight's admin: copy assignments into a spreadsheet. Again.
dayInTheLife.after0: Open Strummy. See everyone you're teaching today, what they worked on, what broke.
dayInTheLife.after1: Progress report drafted from lesson notes. Send in one click.
dayInTheLife.after2: "Blackbird" is in the shared library, tabs attached, marked as started.
dayInTheLife.after3: Lesson starts. Last session's notes are already on screen.
dayInTheLife.after4: You're done. Admin happened automatically during the day.

features.feature0Body: Profiles, lesson history, repertoire, skill progression, and practice streaks — yours or your students', all on one page. The thing you kept meaning to build in Notion.
features.feature1Title: Schedule it. Run it. Move on.
features.feature1Body: Google Calendar sync means no double-booked 4 o'clocks. Assignments and notes live on every session — when you close it, the record is already written.
features.feature1Alt: Lessons grouped by date with status filters and per-lesson song counts
features.feature2Title: Hundreds of songs, tabs already found.
features.feature2Body: A shared song library with chords, tabs, and streaming links attached. Difficulty ratings. One click to add to your repertoire — yours or a student's.
features.feature2Bullet2: Add to any repertoire in one click
features.feature2Alt: Song library with difficulty levels, musical keys, and author filters
features.feature3Body: Any scale or chord, any key — mapped and coloured across all six strings, with interval labels against the root. Tap a fret to name the note. Runs in any browser.
features.feature3Bullet0: Every scale and chord, in every key
features.feature3Bullet2: Tap a note to identify it
features.feature3Alt: Interactive fretboard mapping A minor pentatonic across all six strings

featureShotPanels.lessonNoteQuote: “Alternating bass pattern is solid at 60 BPM. Right-hand independence is the next hurdle — fingerpicking drill 10 min/day.”

strips.worksWithHeadline: The tools you already live in.

founder.headlinePrefix: Built by a guitar teacher who was
founder.quote: “I teach guitar in Warsaw — twenty-odd students, mostly weekly lessons. For years the record of what each of them was working on lived in chat threads and my own memory. I built Strummy because I didn't want to reconstruct it every Thursday anymore. I'm still teaching. I still use it every day.”
founder.photoAlt: Piotr, Strummy's founder, playing acoustic guitar in a park

betaCard.headline: Free while we're in beta. All features included.
betaCard.body: No cards on file, no feature gates, no surprise upsells. When paid tiers launch, beta users keep access to everything they’re using at a permanent discount.

finalCta.body: Start free. No credit card. Practicing solo or teaching twenty students — Strummy scales to however you play.

footer.tagline: A quieter kind of software for learning and teaching guitar. Built in Warsaw by a working guitar teacher.
